entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: KORD: Breaking the Key-Generation Bottleneck in Dealerless Function Secret Sharing via Protocol–Hardware Co-Design
entry.summary:
Function secret sharing (FSS) has emerged as a promising technique for secure multi-party computation (MPC), offering a lightweight online phase. However, existing FSS-based private inference frameworks typically rely on trusted dealers to generate and distribute large amounts of offline key material (e.g., 16.8 GiB for BERT-base), incurring substantial overhead in key generation, transfer, storage, and parsing. Cryptographic dealer-free FSS eliminates the trusted dealer but introduces costly interaction during key generation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Pufferfish: DAG-Guided Speculative Execution for Low-Latency BFT SMR
entry.summary:
Modern Byzantine fault-tolerant state machine replication (BFT SMR) systems increasingly decouple data dissemination from transaction ordering, but typically execute transactions only after consensus finalizes their order. This execution-after-consensus design serializes ordering and execution on the confirmation path, so transactions incur both costs even under normal network conditions. Decoupling enables dissemination to continue during ordering stalls, but amplifies the same bottleneck: disseminated transactions accumulate into an execution backlog that replicas must drain after ordering recovers.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems #consensus

entry.title: Independent Leakage Does Not Save Evasive LWE: Refuting Folklore Fixes in the Private-Coin Setting
entry.summary:
The evasive learning with errors (evasive LWE) assumption has enabled a wide range of advanced cryptographic constructions from lattices in the past few years. The simple intuition that LWE remains secure even when additional ``non-zeroizing'' short preimages are given has proved highly versatile in applications. Unfortunately, recent counterexamples have refuted its general private-coin formulations, showing that having the short preimages along with arbitrary auxiliary leakage about the secret and target matrices can invalidate this intuition.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Superlattice methods for the shortest vector problem and discrete Gaussian sampling
entry.summary:
We give worst-case algorithms for the shortest vector problem (SVP) and discrete Gaussian sampling (DGS) at arbitrary widths. Both algorithms generate lists on a dense superlattice and combine vectors along a chain down to the input lattice. Random shifts let us control the expected number of representations of a vector regardless of the lattice.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: On the Number of Restricted Solutions to Constrained Systems and their Applications
entry.summary:
In this paper, we formulate a special class of systems of linear equations over finite fields that appears naturally in the provable security analysis of several MAC and PRF modes of operation. We derive lower bounds on the number of solutions for such systems adhering to some predefined restrictions, and apply these lower bounds to derive tight PRF security for several constructions. We show security up to $2^{3n/4}$ queries for the single-keyed variant of the Double-block Hash-then-Sum (DBHtS) construction, called 1k-DBHtS, under appropriate assumptions on the underlying hash function.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Masked Solving of Linear Equations System and Application to UOV Signatures
entry.summary:
In response to the looming quantum threat, NIST has selected four algorithms for standardization (i.e., ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and FN-DSA), yet three of the four schemes are based on Euclidean lattices, which raises concerns about the mathematical diversity of post-quantum algorithms. NIST has therefore announced an additional call for post-quantum signatures with a preference for schemes constructed from assumptions other than lattices. Among such candidates, the Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) signature over the multivariate quadratic (MQ) problem is attractive for its short signature and security against quantum cryptanalysis.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Practical SNARGs for Matrix Multiplications over Encrypted Data. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computations to be performed directly on encrypted data, without ever requiring decryption.
entry.summary:
Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computations to be performed directly on encrypted data, without ever requiring decryption. This capability is particularly crucial for privacy-preserving outsourced computation in sensitive fields such as healthcare and finance. While FHE ensures data confidentiality under the honest-but-curious adversarial model, achieving full malicious security, encompassing both integrity and privacy, requires an additional layer of verifiability.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
